QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_38

question.text: When aggregate open interest in a stock derivative across exchanges exceeds 95% of the Market Wide Position Limit (MWPL):

answer.text: No fresh positions are permitted from the subsequent trading day; only exposure-reducing/square-off trades are allowed until aggregate open outstanding position falls to 80% or below
Trading in that stock derivative is halted completely

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the source, when aggregate open interest across exchanges exceeds 95% of MWPL, no fresh positions are permitted from the subsequent trading day. Only exposure-reducing/square-off trades are allowed, and normal trading resumes only when the aggregate open outstanding position falls to 80% or below. The Trap: Trading is not halted entirely - existing positions can be closed. The trigger is "exceeds 95%" (not "reaches 95%"), the restriction takes effect from the subsequent trading day, and the resumption threshold is 80% of MWPL. Note: Source: NISM-Series-VIII workbook (Dec 2025), pages 168, 170 and 179.
